newsitem.title: UK: UK's Smith not satisfied with Camelot pay plans.
newsitem.headline: UK's Smith not satisfied with Camelot pay plans.

text.p: National Heritage Secretary Chris Smith said on Monday he was not satisfied with the proposals on pay made by national lottery operator Camelot aimed at defusing a controversy over big bonuses.
Earlier, Camelot chairman Sir George Russell offered to pay out of the company's own profits a sum to charity equivalent to hefty bonuses paid to the firm's directors last year.
"That's welcome but frankly it's a sideshow because it doesn't address the point of major public concern, which is the level of remuneration going to the directors," Smith told reporters.

"The directors' remuneration would remain completely untouched and I don't find that acceptable. I want to see some or all of the bonuses that they've received going to charity and I want a commitment that that will happen for future amounts as well," he added.
Camelot said they would consider his demand but gave him no commitment. Smith said he expected a response from Camelot by the end of the week.
Russell earlier said Camelot had offered to work with the government on ways of turning the lottery into a not-for-profit organisation before the firm's contract expires in 2001.
Aspects of this examination would include directors' remuneration, he said.
"We are saying we are prepared to look at the shape (of the lottery) to get it to a non-profit-making contract during that time," Russell said.

Asked whether he expected to see a not-for-profit lottery running before 2001, Smith responded: "There's a racing certainty that from 2001 onwards we will have a lottery that's run sensibly on a not-for-profit basis."
Russell said he had agreed with Smith that Camelot would forego interest to which it is contractually entitled on money waiting to be paid out of its prize fund.
Interest on the shortfall between prize money allocated by Camelot and money won by lottery players is worth about six million pounds to Camelot.
"We've agreed that we would be willing to waive that subject to discussions with the director general (of the lottery)," Russell said.
Russell, who called the meeting with Smith "very constructive", said he would discuss with Camelot directors the subject of their long-term incentive bonus scheme.
